cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I crossed out two o'clock like you and told everyone three. That's my part of the empty meeting room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cross meant I couldn't attend at two. I didn't change the meeting time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, checking availability. I should have sent a proper update. What did you do with the room booking?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Moved it upstairs. The ground-floor room had a leak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I've admitted the late message. Add your upstairs move to it, and we can send one explanation with both our names.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copied diary cancellation becomes B2 availability correction; A3 covers while admitting poor update, but A5 calls it a late message without establishing lateness.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no-time-change causes A3 notification admission; B4 room move supplies A5 joint account, but the exact admitted fault shifts.

relationship.evidence: B4 gives a concrete reason for moving the room.

heightening.evidence: A5 combines two mistakes, but B4 move itself is not confessed as unannounced, and A's late-message fact is new.

specificity.evidence: A1 says told everyone three; A3 says should send update; A5 says late without chronology.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 one explanation/both names is usable after the admission facts are made coherent.
